label: first copy step (input = fed-back first token, right after <DEL>), long sequences
explanation: Fires almost only at the step right after <DEL>, when the first original token comes back as input and the second is being output (recall_idx==1 gets 97% of mass, 94% of activations). Never fires in the original phase. Weak tail at <DEL> itself (1.8% of mass) and recall_idx 2 (1%). Within recall_idx==1, firing rate and size go up steeply with L: about 0 for L<=4, rate 0.5 at L=9, with L=9 giving 68% of mass. The input token identity also matters: b is by far the strongest (top activations are nearly all b or z first tokens), then z, h, u, e, 0. Neither L nor token alone separates active from inactive steps, so precision stays low (0.31 for L>=8). Restricting to the top tokens raises precision to ~0.7 but recall drops to 0.36.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: b, z, h, u, e, 0; least: a, t, i, o) and the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: u, n, c, q; copy phase: u, t, y, p; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=9 & t=10, L=9 & t=9.
